figures.finding: There is no VAT; the BIR administers a gross receipts tax on business receipts.
figures.applies: Rate and exemption threshold not confirmed; see blocker.

figures.finding: The gross receipts tax is 5% of total business receipts with no deduction for costs: a business with annual receipts of USD 225,000 or more pays 5% on all of them and files monthly (30 days after the month); one under 225,000 pays 5% only on receipts above USD 9,000 in each month (an unused month's exemption lapses) and files annually by 30 January.

value.asOf: BIR tax structure booklet (2022 file); a change since not checked

figures.applies: Business receipts in the USVI (V.I. Code title 33, chapter 3)

sources.said: In General. The Virgin Islands gross receipts tax is a tax on total receipts from the conduct of a business within the Virgin Islands, without reduction for cost of goods sold or services or any other expenses. … 1. Those businesses with annual gross receipts of $225,000 or more, and 2. Those businesses with annual gross receipts of less than $225,000. Businesses in the first category pay a tax of five percent on their entire gross receipts, while businesses in the second category pay a tax of five percent on receipts in excess of $9,000 per month. The $9,000–per–month exemption is lost if not used in one month. … Businesses with gross receipts of more than $225,000 per year are required to file monthly reports on Form 720V.I. The returns are due 30 days following the last day of the month concerned. Businesses with gross receipts of $225,000 or less per year are required to file an annual report with the BIR by the 30th day following the last day of the year concerned on Form 720-B.
